newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria has $33.7 mln Jan-Sept current account gap.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria has $33.7 mln Jan-Sept current account gap.

text.p: Bulgaria posted a current account deficit of $33.7 million in the first nine months of this year after a $103.2 million surplus for the same period of 1995, preliminary Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) figures show.
BULGARIA CURRENT ACCOUNT Jan-Sept Jan-June Jan-Sept'95
Exports fell 15.6 percent year-on-year for the first nine months while imports decreased by 13.7 percent.
Exports declined due to lower foreign demand, ongoing slide in industrial output, high interest rates, restructuring of the industrial and financial sectors and rising energy prices, the BNB said.

Imports fell mainly due to the sharp depreciation of the lev currency against the dollar, declining purchasing power of companies and individuals, and an additional import tax of five percent, in force since June 4.
The Bulgarian lev fell to 235-240 per dollar at the end of September from around 71 at the beginning of 1996.

BNB's central interest rate rose to 300 percent annually in September from 34 percent in January while cumulative inflation for the first nine months was 153 percent. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-876032
